Triage: lands in `packages/i18n/src/locales/de.ts` (plus, under option 2, one row of `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`) ⇒ **`domain:ui`**. Type **Bug**, and the type is not a close call: `Ablehne…` is not a grammatical German form. `ablehnen` is separable, so the first-person singular is *ich lehne ab* — the pack ships broken German to users today. The card says it plainly: either way `Ablehne…` should not survive.

⛔ **Stale premise, corrected**: both this card and #6610 state "#5972 … remains open on its own." **#5972 closed at 2026-08-27T13:54:21Z**, roughly 27 minutes after this card was filed. That cuts in this card's favour rather than against it — the `LOADING_GROUP_FORKS` exemption row and the converged in-group members are now landed facts in the tree rather than pending ones — but whoever picks this up should read the pin from the tree, ⛔ not from this card's description of it.

**`pm:queue`, not the decision inbox.** The card presents a fork, but the escalation threshold is not met: an existing, measured convention in the codebase settles it. The `de` pack's dominant register for in-flight states is the passive (37 values whose `en` is a bare gerund render as `Wird …`), and this screen is the island. So — **ruled toward option 2** (move the screen to the passive: `Genehmige…` → `Wird genehmigt…`, `Ablehne…` → `Wird abgelehnt…`, `Lade…` → `Wird geladen…`, and delete the exemption row). It is the option that removes a permanent carve-out rather than maintaining one, and a maintained exemption row is a trap every later agent must read and preserve.

⇒ **Premise the dev verifies first, ⛔ not a fence**: *the `de` pack's dominant in-flight register is the passive, at roughly 37 values.* Re-count it against the tree. If that dominance does not hold, the basis for option 2 is gone — **stop and report the fork**, do not silently fall back to option 1 and do not proceed on the card's number. Option 1 (keep first person, `Ablehne…` → `Lehne ab…`, exemption row stays with an updated reason) is the fallback the seat re-decides on, not the dev's to pick.

⚠️ **Serial constraint — shared hot file with #6610.** Both cards were spun out of #5972, both land in `packages/i18n/src/locales/*`, and **both touch `ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`**. That collision has to be answered explicitly by the dispatching seat rather than defaulted to serial by omission. This seat's read of the five fold gates, offered as input and ⛔ not as the dispatch decision: ① same defect shape (one pack renders one concept two ways) and same fix method (normalise values, then adjust/widen the pin) — yes; ② same package and same pin file, so one worktree, one changeset, one queue slot — yes; ③ both graded this round, neither in the decision inbox — yes; ④ independently checkable (this card: the three `auth.device.*` values and the deleted row; #6610: the 8 `ar` values) — yes; ⑤ **exclusion list**: ⛔ #5972 itself is *not* a family member — it is closed and was fenced to the ten byte-identical `Loading…` keys; and no other locale's divergence is in scope, because none has been measured.

⇒ Five gates read as passing, so folding these two into one dispatch looks correct. The call is the objectui seat's.

Scope confirmed as filed: 1–3 values plus at most one pin row; no key added or removed, no `en` value moves.

Dispatching on triage's 2026-08-27 ruling toward **option 2**, unchanged. Recording the seat decisions triage explicitly left to it, plus two facts newer than that ruling.

## ⛔ The fold question is answered by events: dispatched ALONE, not folded

Triage read the five fold gates as passing and left the call here. It is now moot in the direction that resolves it cleanly: **#6610 has already landed** — PR #6675 merged at 14:05Z today and closed it. So the shared hot file resolves by **sequencing rather than folding**, which is the better outcome anyway: one card, one queue slot, one reviewable change.

⇒ ⛔ The dev must not fold #6610 in, and must not re-verify or re-touch the `ar` work. It is done and on `main`.

## ⚠️ `ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts` moved under this card less than an hour ago

PR #6675 **edited that exact file** — it rewrote the `ar` note, because that note's present-tense claim had just become false. Option 2 requires deleting the `LOADING_GROUP_FORKS` exemption row from the *same* file.

⇒ Read it from a ref that includes `fff964510`. ⛔ Any line number or file content written about it before 14:05Z today describes a different file. Branch from current `origin/main`, not from an older base.

⚠️ While in there: that file's group check **derives** its population from `en` (`value === 'Loading…'`) and asserts the derived set equals its ten named keys. `auth.device.loading` is one of the ten and its `en` value does not change here, so converging its `de` value must leave that derivation green. If deleting the exemption row moves the derived set, **stop** — something other than this card is wrong.

## The premise to verify first — ⛔ this is a premise, not a fence

Triage's basis for option 2 is a measured convention: **the `de` pack's dominant in-flight register is the passive, at roughly 37 values whose `en` is a bare gerund rendering as `Wird …`.** Re-count that against the tree.

⛔ If the dominance does not hold, the basis for option 2 is gone: **stop and report the fork.** Do not silently fall back to option 1, and do not proceed on the card's number without re-deriving it. Option 1 is the fallback **this seat** re-decides on — it is not the dev's to pick. Quoting triage: *"Option 1 … is the fallback the seat re-decides on, not the dev's to pick."*

## Also stale in the card's own body

Both this card and #6610 say "#5972 … remains open on its own." **#5972 closed 2026-08-27T13:54:21Z**, ~27 minutes after this card was filed. Triage already corrected it, and it cuts in this card's favour — the exemption row and the converged in-group members are landed facts in the tree, not pending ones. ⛔ Read the pin from the tree, not from this card's description of it.

## Scope

`Genehmige…` → `Wird genehmigt…`, `Ablehne…` → `Wird abgelehnt…`, `Lade…` → `Wird geladen…` in `packages/i18n/src/locales/de.ts`, plus deleting the one exemption row. No key added or removed, no `en` value moves, no other locale touched.

Graded **Bug** and it is not a close call: `ablehnen` is a separable-prefix verb, so the first-person singular is *ich lehne ab* — `Ablehne…` is not a grammatical German form and the pack ships it to users today. Either option kills it; option 2 also removes a permanent carve-out rather than maintaining one, and a maintained exemption row is a trap every later agent must read and preserve.

ACCEPT — PR #6685, head `817a615e5`, flipped ready; auto-merge follows its table.

Landed as triage ruled: option 2, the passive register. `Genehmige…` → `Wird genehmigt…`, `Ablehne…` → `Wird abgelehnt…`, `Lade…` → `Wird geladen…`, and the `LOADING_GROUP_FORKS` exemption row deleted.

## ⭐ The premise was re-derived first, and the instrument was built properly

This was the one thing the dispatch made conditional, and it was done before anything was touched — Unicode-aware (`\p{L}`, `u` flag) and **position-aware** (`en` matching a bare-gerund shape, `de` matching passive-first-word), with a **positive control** (`common.loading`: `Loading…` / `Wird geladen…`, both matched) so a zero or a surprising number would have been distinguishable from a broken query.

Result: **40 of 61** `en`-bare-gerund keys render `de` passively (~66%) against 21 that do not — and all three `auth.device.*` keys are correctly among the 21 pre-fix. Triage said "roughly 37"; the measured number is 40.

⭐ Worth naming: the dev reported *"close to triage's roughly 37; dominance holds either way"* rather than quietly adopting the card's number or quietly substituting its own. The premise the ruling rested on is what mattered, not the digit, and it held — so option 2 proceeded on a re-derived basis rather than an inherited one.

## The pin file was handled with more care than "delete the row"

Deleting the exemption row is the mechanical part. The dev also:

- updated the length assertion (1 → 0),
- **removed the two trailing assertions that pinned the fork's first-person reason** — those statements are now false, and leaving them would have left the file asserting something untrue about a fork that no longer exists,
- moved the JSDoc block documenting the fork to past tense with a resolved-by pointer.

⭐ And it named its own precedent correctly: *"same class of edit PR #6675 made to this file's `ar` note today."* That is the right read — #6675 rewrote that note for exactly the same reason, a present-tense claim that had become false. Two devs, same file, same day, same discipline, without coordination.

⚠️ The gate interaction the dispatch flagged came back green and was checked explicitly: the #5972 group-derivation test passes, because `auth.device.loading`'s `en` value never moved. The derived set is unchanged; only `de`'s rendering converged.

## Ablation — predicted, and predicted *precisely*

The prediction was not just "it goes red" but **which** key and **why**: only `auth.device.loading` is a `LOADING_GROUP` member (`approving` / `denying` sit outside it), so reverting that one alone should red the #5972 uniformity test naming it, now that `LOADING_GROUP_FORKS` is empty.

Observed exactly that: `de: 2 renderings — "Wird geladen…" on … | "Lade…" on auth.device.loading`, 6/7 passed, 1/7 failed, exit 1.

⭐ Mutation proved on disk by **anchor counts, not `git diff --stat`** — and the dev said why, which is the part that shows it understood the trap: this is an equal-length substitution, so a size check would have proven nothing. `"Wird geladen…"` 8 → 7, `loading: "Lade…"` 0 → 1. Restore proved by observation (`git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --short` clean, anchor counts back to 8), then the pin re-run green on the restored tree — ⛔ not by an exit code.

⭐ One NOT-MEASURED handled correctly: `type-check` first failed with **TS6305** from stale `core`/`types` `dist/*.d.ts`. That is a missing precondition, not a red — the dev built the closure and re-ran to exit 0.

`check-i18n-en-drift`: `No en value changed in this range.` No key added or removed, no other locale touched, `Ablehne…` gone.
